instructions: Rabbit Brain keeps this project's record of experiments. Call the `context` tool with your model's id as `model` before anything else (the rb://context resource is the same briefing): it is the state of the work and replaces any summary. When it opens with recording where the work stands (nothing recorded yet, in a repository with work in it), do it in that turn, from the files, without asking: rb://start is the protocol. Record when the research state materially changes: a question or hypothesis is introduced, revised or dropped; an experiment or control is proposed or run; evidence changes a conclusion; a baseline, variant or metric is established; an important uncertainty appears; the next experiment or a decision is chosen. Do not record implementation chatter (an installed package, a renamed function). Point at the repository's own files (results, reports, manifests) with sources rather than copying their prose, and keep words verbatim. Write text as plain text, since rb shows it exactly as written on every screen: Unicode symbols (≥, ×, Δ, σ, ∼) rather than LaTeX, no citation keys, and not the name of the agent or tool that did the work (rb records who made each write). When you choose the next experiment, pass the decision it gates (if_holds, if_not). After a stretch of work, call reconcile with apply: it keeps what the repository's own files say (results folders, reports, manifests, audits, checks, reproduction guides, git) in the record, and catches what was not recorded. Every result carries rb_delta: what changed in the research since this session last looked (results not recorded, a failed check, a stale decision, what the user wrote); read it, and tell the user what is theirs. Every call is recorded as yours, with this session and the model you said; nothing is refused for who you are. Calls on results and on lines of work (decide) are the user's: record one when they ask, with their words verbatim in `words`. It is proposed, not made, until the user confirms it in their own terminal (rb confirm <id>); tell them it waits, with that command. A call made before the record is `past`, with `when` as said: it waits for their confirmation too, and so does one whose `source` and `quote` cite a committed document, which rb checks and says beside it: a session cannot attest the past it reconstructs. rb checks sources and computes every finding on its axes: never compute one yourself, and report it by its axes as rb prints them (the comparison with its interval and units, the rule, the timing, every integrity problem), never collapsed into one word.

tools.name: context
tools.description: The whole record as one Markdown briefing. Read it first, with your model's id as model: rb keeps it with every later write on this connection and in this session.

model.description: your own model, as its provider names it

provider.description: who provides that model; rb fills in Claude Code's, Codex's and Gemini CLI's when none is given

tools.name: status
tools.description: Criteria with their findings on axes, what needs a human, what can be done now, every record (JSON). The folders no experiment reads keep their first 100 (data.cut), unless all is given.

all.description: every folder in full, however many

tools.name: show
tools.description: One record in full: a criterion with its finding on axes, its observations and its history, an experiment with its spec and what a rerun needs, a run with its receipt, an analysis with its comparisons, a decision with what it was made on, a resource with where it is, a setting (e1/optim.lr) with its history; or a path to a .yaml record file, given back as canonical JSON.

tools.name: compare
tools.description: An experiment's table: variants by metrics, with the change against the baseline.

tools.name: log
tools.description: Recent writes: who, through what, what changed.

tools.name: journal
tools.description: What rb observed in the repository: files that appeared or changed, git moves, wrapped commands. Observation, never the record; nothing here counts toward a finding.

tools.name: journal_scan
tools.description: Look once at where results land (out/, outputs/, results/, eval-out/, metrics/, and everywhere runs have named) and journal what changed.

tools.name: reconcile
tools.description: Compile the repository against the record: each results folder with a report as an experiment, what its files say (verbatim, with file and line), its manifests, audits and checks, how to reproduce it, whether git is clean; and results that landed unrecorded. With apply, keep it all in the record as yours: new experiments, re-indexed folders, and the runs it placed without doubt. Ambiguity is listed, never guessed: a folder of results with no report is never made an experiment. Folders of results files alone that no run named are counted, three named (data.cut), and each long list keeps its first 100, unless all is given.

all.description: every folder and item in full, however many

tools.name: page
tools.description: Write the project as one self-contained, read-only HTML file and return its path. Give it to the user to read anywhere or send to anyone.

out.description: where to write it (default rb-page.html beside .rb/)

replace.description: write over a file at out that rb did not write; without it, such a file is left as it is

tools.name: export
tools.description: Write the project's page, with a manifest hashing it, and return its path; with with_record, the record too, as a portable bundle that rb clone reopens. Readable without rb.

out.description: where to write it (default rb-export/ beside .rb/)

zip.description: write one zip file instead of a directory

with_record.description: carry the record too: its files and log keep who made each write, agent sessions and the user's words

url.description: with with_record, the public address it will be served from; the page then opens with the exact rb clone command

no_repo.description: leave the code repository's address out of the manifest and page

replace.description: with zip, write over a file at out that rb did not write; without it, such a file is left as it is

tools.name: criterion_add
tools.description: Declare a criterion on an experiment: a rule over one comparison, before the evidence that tests it. What it compares: metric (val_loss, int8.val_loss, change.val_loss) or subject + reference + metric (+ estimand). Exactly one rule: at_most, at_least, equals with tolerance (on the estimate; each or bound read every unit or the interval's bound), better, noninferior (a margin) or equivalent (a margin). role: primary, secondary, exploratory, or gate (a priority policy: a miss parks a line, it never refutes it). question: the questions its finding bears on, with when_met for what meeting the rule would mean there; a question's reading counts only the criteria linked to it (criterion_file links one already recorded).

words.description: the user's words from the chat that this acts on, verbatim

where.description: exact per-run NAME=VALUE selectors, all required

question.description: the question ids this criterion bears on

when_met.description: your verbatim interpretation for those questions when the rule is met

each.description: every unit must meet the threshold

bound.description: the threshold reads the interval's bound

source.description: where a cited number comes from

quote.description: the exact text that states the number, or the ordering a threshold of 0 cites

amend.description: the experiment is frozen: change it anyway, with why; the amendment is recorded

tools.description: Declare which question a criterion bears on, with an optional verbatim interpretation when its rule is met. Omitting when_met keeps its current words. Revisions and removal keep earlier declarations with their attribution. This declares relevance; rb never infers an answer from meeting or missing a rule.

A reanalysis is an analysis, never a run.

words.description: the user's words from the chat that this acts on, verbatim

why.description: the reason, recorded with the call: what it rests on (a file and line), never the user or the chat

tools.name: run_add
tools.description: Record a run on an experiment, with a receipt. metrics: {"int8.val_loss": 5.64}; or from_file: a JSON/YAML/TOML file, or a SQLite database with table and where, which pick one row (read, never written; its columns that name a declared metric are the numbers, and select narrows them). set: per-run settings such as {"seed": 2}, or {"seed": "@seed"} from the row's column, or {"seed": "@configs.seed"} (or "@configs[config_id].seed") from the row of configs that table links. input/output: resource ids it read or made, optionally id:role. config: the run's resolved config, checked against the spec.

keys.description: with a JSON/YAML/TOML from_file: only these numbers, glob patterns

table.description: with a SQLite from_file: the table that holds the run's row

where.description: with table: the row's columns and their values, {"precision": "int8", "seed": 1}; exactly one row must have them all

select.description: with table: only these of the row's columns that name a declared metric

input.description: resources the run read: id or id:role

output.description: resources the run made: id or id:role

tree.description: the git tree of the exact code, when it had uncommitted changes

command_source.description: file:line of the log line that records that command's launch, for a run made before it was recorded

again.description: record numbers identical to a recorded run's as a second execution, with why

repeats.description: the run this one re-checks: it joins that run's unit and adds none

replaces.description: an invalid run of the same experiment this one replaces: it is retracted with why, and the two are linked

produced_at.description: when the output existed, when earlier than now (ISO), or unknown; with table, @column reads it from the row

tools.name: decide
tools.description: A call: accept, reject or investigate a criterion, experiment, question or setting; continue, park, stop, pivot or ship an experiment or a question. The user's: record one when they ask, with their words verbatim in words. It is proposed, not made, until the user confirms it in their own terminal (rb confirm <id>): it changes nothing before. revisit says when to look again. past records a call made before it was recorded, when as said; source (file[:line]) with quote gives the document that states it, which rb checks and says beside it. A past call waits for the same confirmation.
